title: Freya and the Choir
premise: Sable Sandoval has spent a lifetime keeping the Thornfell gate sealed and their name off every ledger, guiding smugglers and fugitives through the mountains while the kingdom above pretends the old gods are dead. But when prayers begin to be answered—crops blooming overnight, the sick rising from beds—the god beneath the gate wakes, and it is not the gentle deity of the hymns: it is the thing that unmade the last king, now wearing the current king like a glove. Sable, whose bloodline was bound to the gate as jailers, must choose between the loyalty they owe the smuggler network that raised them and the truth that one of their own has been feeding souls to the crown. With the help of a disgraced priestess, Isolde Vane, and a smuggler captain who loves them, Sable descends into the god's prison to unbind the king before the coronation rite completes at midwinter. They succeed only by taking the binding into themselves, becoming the new keeper of a living gate—and choosing, finally, to be seen.
about_author: Marguerite Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore in the northern ranges before turning to fiction. She writes about gates, oaths, and the people paid to keep both shut, and lives somewhere with poor cell reception on purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine smuggling run through the Thornfell passes establishes Sable's world: the hidden roads, the tolls, the careful anonymity. But a dying courier delivers a prayer-scarred token that hums against the gate stones. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in a life built on staying invisible.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Answers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In a valley village, Sable witnesses a answered prayer—a blind child seeing—and realizes the old gods are listening again. The villagers credit the king's new piety. Sable knows better: nothing answers from above the snowline except what's under the gate. Beat: dread disguised as wonder.

chapters.title: Isolde Vane, Defrocked
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. A former priestess of the suppressed order works in a border infirmary, secretly still praying. When her prayers start working too well—a patient rises wrong-eyed—she flees toward Thornfell, following the token's call. Beat: guilt sharpening into purpose; she knows what answering gods cost last time.

chapters.title: The Gatekeeper's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable opens the family vault beneath the waystation and finds their grandmother's journal: the Sandovals were not smugglers' guides but jailers, and the 'gate' is a mouth. The binding weakens each generation. Beat: inheritance reframed as sentence, not gift.

chapters.title: Captain Renn of the Low Road
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. The smuggler captain who loves Sable notices the changed routes and the token's glow. Loyal to his crew and to Sable, he agrees to move supplies for whatever's coming without asking questions—yet. Beat: warmth and loyalty established, with the first lie of omission between them.

chapters.title: A Crown That Prays Back
chapters.summary: Court interlude, Isolde's POV via a captured letter and a pilgrim's account. King Aldric has grown radiant, beloved, terrifyingly generous—and the coronation renewal rite approaches at midwinter. Those who pray to him directly stop sleeping. Beat: the antagonist revealed obliquely; scale widens from mountain to kingdom.

chapters.title: The Traitor Among the Tolls
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Someone in the network has been leaving offerings at the gate—names written in blood-ink, souls prepaid. Sable traces the handwriting to Maro, the man who taught them the passes. Beat: betrayal lands hardest because it wears a mentor's face; loyalty vs. truth begins its argument.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Sable and Maro, then Renn arriving mid-fight. Maro claims he's saving the network: the god offers protection the kingdom never gave them. He escapes with the ledger of names. Renn learns what Sable has hidden. Beat: rupture—Sable loses mentor and nearly loses Renn in one night.

chapters.title: Isolde Arrives
chapters.summary: Isolde reaches the waystation half-frozen, carrying proof of the rite's mechanics: the king must be unbound before the crown touches the relic at midwinter or the merge becomes permanent. She and Sable form an uneasy alliance. Beat: reluctant partnership; two keepers of different broken oaths.

chapters.title: The Descent Road
chapters.summary: Sable, Isolde, and Renn take the smugglers' deepest route toward the prison beneath the gate. Trials along the way: collapsing passages, prayers whispered by the mountain itself, temptations tailored to each traveler. Beat: rising tension; the mountain tests whether they're rescuers or offerings.

chapters.title: Maro's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maro's POV. At the threshold, Maro bargains with the god-thing, offering the ledger of names to speed the king's full possession in exchange for dominion over the free roads. We see his logic fully—he believes he's protecting his people. Beat: villain humanized; justice outside the law given a face.

chapters.title: Voices Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Deep in the prison, Sable hears the bound dead—including their grandmother, who reveals the original sin: the first Sandoval didn't imprison the god, they invited it, and every keeper since has fed it just enough to stay quiet. Beat: the family myth collapses; grief and fury fused.

chapters.title: Renn's Choice
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. The god offers Renn his drowned crewmates back, whole. He refuses—but barely, and he tells Sable so. Their honesty rebuilds trust on harder ground. Beat: loyalty vs. truth resolved personally before it can be resolved politically.

chapters.title: The Kingdom Above
chapters.summary: Interlude, multiple brief POVs via pilgrims and soldiers. Midwinter approaches; the capital glows with unnatural prosperity while dissidents vanish. Isolde's old order is being resurrected—as the god's mouthpiece. Beat: stakes made national; the clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Maro's Fall
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable catches Maro completing the final offering and defeats him—not by killing him but by burning the ledger, freeing the named souls and stripping his bargain. Maro, emptied, chooses to stay below. Beat: justice outside the law enacted; mercy as weapon.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Using her defrocked order's forbidden liturgy, Isolde begins separating king from god while Sable holds the gate's mouth open and Renn guards the passage. The thing fights with memories, wearing faces they love. Beat: climax begins; every theme converges in ritual.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The god offers Sable the ultimate temptation: restore the Sandoval name to honor, make the mountains safe forever, if they let it keep the king. Sable refuses and speaks the true name their grandmother hid. Beat: the moral climax—truth chosen over every comfortable lie.

chapters.title: Midwinter
chapters.summary: Climax. The rite tears the god from King Aldric, but the gate needs a living anchor or the thing escapes entirely. Sable takes the binding into themselves as the crown touches the relic. Beat: sacrifice at the exact deadline; the chapter ends on whiteout silence.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn carries an unconscious Sable up the descent road while Isolde stabilizes the half-bound gate. The king wakes in the capital with no memory of three years. Beat: exhausted tenderness; survival uncertain, change certain.

chapters.title: What Is Owed
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde negotiates with the recovering court: no restoration of her order, no hunt for smugglers, amnesty for the network—in exchange for silence about what really happened. Justice arranged outside the law's machinery. Beat: bittersweet pragmatism; the themes cashed out.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Is Seen
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Awake, carrying the god quietly inside the gate's new binding, Sable walks openly into the valley village that once ignored them, and signs their name—for the first time—to a ledger anyone can read. Beat: resolution of invisibility; inheritance transformed into chosen duty.

chapters.title: Freya and the Choir
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating POVs. Spring comes to Thornfell. The old gods answer small prayers again—honest ones, kept small by the keeper's discipline. Renn stays; Isolde teaches; Maro's empty cell below stays dark. Sable listens at the gate each night and hears, faintly, something almost like singing. Beat: peace earned, vigilance permanent, hope qualified.
